items.title: Dosage of an antibody-drug conjugate

drug_mapping.basis: Original patent ADC (1) = DS-1062a and NCT03401385 / DS1062-A-J101; official NCI and ClinicalTrials.gov explicitly connect the same codes to datopotamab deruxtecan. No later secondary patent cross-reference is required.

sources.availability_basis: Conservative retrieval timestamp; historical webpage version not verified
Conservative retrieval timestamp; historical registry versions not fetched

document_evidence.observation: ADC (1) uses heavy-chain SEQ ID NO 45 and light-chain SEQ ID NO 46; DAR 3.5–4.5. ADC (2), DAR 6.5–8.0, must not be substituted.
Antibody-drug conjugate (1) is explicitly also referred to as DS-1062a.
First-in-human DS-1062a study explicitly identifies NCT03401385.
Study DS1062-A-J101; cutoff 2019-11-16. 95 treated; 88 response evaluable. 6 mg/kg: 5/18, 27.8%, 95% CI 9.7–53.5. 8 mg/kg: 13/34, 38.2%, 95% CI 22.2–56.4. Investigator-assessed unconfirmed responses.
Response evaluable requires baseline and post-baseline assessment, or treatment discontinuation; confidence intervals are exact Clopper-Pearson.

experiment_cards.extraction_method: OCR extraction with AI visual comparison against original PDF page
experiment_cards.title: 一期 DS-1062a 研究中的未确认客观缓解率
experiment_cards.experiment_system: Phase 1 open-label dose escalation/expansion; 6 mg/kg escalation cohort; 8 mg/kg escalation and expansion cohorts; response-evaluable analysis set
experiment_cards.species_or_cell: Human participants with previously treated NSCLC
missing_fields: Full sequence alignment against regulatory INN reference
experiment_cards.source_location: PDF page 93, printed page 91, Example 7, paragraphs [0455]-[0458], Table 2
experiment_cards.source_excerpt: 5/18 subjects with response, all with PR; 13/34, all with PR.
experiment_cards.interpretation_limit: This is a patent-reported, early-phase, nonrandomized, unconfirmed response outcome. It is not a phase 3 treatment effect or a validated forecast.
experiment_cards.response_evaluable_definition: Baseline and post-baseline tumor assessment, or discontinuation of study treatment (PDF p94, paragraph [0459]).

review_gaps: Human scientific review count is zero; the two AI roles share a base model.
The exact identity is verified through explicit development codes and trial identifiers; full sequence alignment to a regulatory INN document has not been performed.
Patent-reported, early-phase, nonrandomized unconfirmed ORR cannot be treated as a phase 3 treatment effect or a validated forecast.
The 88 response-evaluable patients span all reported dose groups; do not use 88 as the denominator for the selected 6 mg/kg (18) or 8 mg/kg (34) groups.
Whole-document OCR is complete but only selected source pages and the selected experiment card were checked; ADC (2) and other unreviewed examples are excluded.
Current NCI and ClinicalTrials.gov identity records are conservatively available only at their recorded retrieval timestamps; do not backdate into historical forecasts.
Official patent-family membership and legal status have not been verified.
No demonstrated incremental prediction accuracy or prospective clinical validation.

reviewers.scope: Primary source alias lookup and original PDF visual verification, including pages 85,87,88,93,94
Independently opened pages 87,88,93,94; checked NCI code names and live ClinicalTrials.gov intervention/alias/program mapping
reviewers.confirmation_basis: Parent collaboration message explicitly confirms each page, dose denominator, ORR, CI, response-evaluable definition and official alias checks

research_review.independence_limit: Two separately executed AI roles share the same base model and may share systematic errors; this is not independent human scientific review.
